builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Triage: Skip, Skim, or Refine Attention Tiles in Video Diffusion Transformers
summary: It replaces full-precision dense attention in video diffusion transformers with a training-free router that assigns each attention tile to skipping (block-mean substitution), NVFP4 computation, or NVFP4 with residual correction, executed by a single fused kernel. It costs the integration effort of a custom kernel, dependence on FP4 tensor-core hardware (RTX Blackwell-class GPUs), and a price hyperparameter that must be set to trade compute against error. It can fail on GPUs without FP4 support (a 24 GB Ada/Ampere card cannot run the reported kernel), on models or resolutions where the error router's predictions misprice tiles, or where the 2.32x figure does not transfer to the reader's specific model and sequence lengths.
rationale: The method is training-free and inference-only, making it directly relevant to production video generation, but its reported gains depend on Blackwell FP4 hardware and per-workload routing behavior, so it warrants a targeted validation on the reader's exact GPU and models before adoption.

claims.statement: It replaces full-precision dense attention in video diffusion transformers with a training-free router that assigns each attention tile to skipping (block-mean substitution), NVFP4 computation, or NVFP4 with residual correction, executed by a single fused kernel. It costs the integration effort of a custom kernel, dependence on FP4 tensor-core hardware (RTX Blackwell-class GPUs), and a price hyperparameter that must be set to trade compute against error. It can fail on GPUs without FP4 support (a 24 GB Ada/Ampere card cannot run the reported kernel), on models or resolutions where the error router's predictions misprice tiles, or where the 2.32x figure does not transfer to the reader's specific model and sequence lengths.
Up to 2.32x end-to-end speedup over dense FlashAttention across Wan2.2, HunyuanVideo, and LTX-2.5, with 0.3-3.0 dB higher PSNR than the strongest baseline in five settings.
